topics.name: Trump Tariffs and Trade War
topics.summary: Comprehensive overview of new US tariffs: 25% on Canadian/Mexican goods, 10% on energy/potash, 25% on global auto imports announced March 26. China retaliating with tariffs on US food. Canada retaliating on $41B in US goods. Ferrari raising prices on some models in response.

topics.name: Defense Tech History and Evolution
topics.summary: Detailed walkthrough from WWII radar technology through Skunk Works, DARPA, the Cold War, the 1993 Last Supper consolidation, the war on terror era (Palantir/SpaceX), and into the current 2020s defense tech startup boom.

topics.name: Defense Tech Investing Bubble
topics.summary: Multiple guests debated whether defense tech is in a bubble, with consensus that there will be significant washout among the 50-60% of companies that can't deliver. The power law is concentrated in a few firms like Anduril, SpaceX. Most VCs who recently entered lack the expertise to diligence hardware failure.

topics.name: Continuing Resolution and DoD Budget
topics.summary: The FY25 continuing resolution lacks a full NDA, limiting net new program starts. However, a key section allows some budget reprogramming. Sophisticated founders are actively identifying unfunded program offices and budget lines. Guests divided on whether this is a crisis or opportunity.

topics.name: Ghibli AI Moment / OpenAI Image Generation
topics.summary: OpenAI's Ghibli-style image filter dominated social media on March 26, 2025. Discussed as a major product moment that may have sherlocked AI image generation competitors like Mid-Journey. Debated as a top signal for the word 'slop' and a potential aesthetic turning point for the internet.

topics.name: US Re-industrialization
topics.summary: Central theme across multiple guests; US manufacturing employment fell from 22% in 1979 to 9% in 2019. Companies like Hadrian, Atomic Industries, and Deterrence are building automated factories to close the manufacturing gap with China, particularly for defense-critical components.

topics.name: NASA Administrator Confirmation / ISS Debate
topics.summary: Jared Isaacman's confirmation as NASA administrator is stalled by Senator Ted Cruz over the ISS deorbit timeline. Elon Musk wants early deorbit; Cruz wants the station maintained through end of decade to protect Texas jobs. NASA is effectively frozen on major program decisions.

topics.name: Cygnus Spacecraft Incident
topics.summary: Northrop Grumman physically dropped the Cygnus cargo spacecraft, forcing a full re-test campaign and rerouting ISS cargo delivery to SpaceX. Cited as further evidence that without SpaceX, the US would have no reliable means of crewing or supplying the ISS.

topics.name: F-47 Next-Generation Air Dominance Fighter
topics.summary: Boeing won the $20B EMD contract for the sixth-generation fighter, a nod to the P-47. The program has been in development for ~10-12 years. Elon Musk opposed human-rated fighters but the Air Force went ahead anyway, demonstrating limits of DOGE influence.

topics.name: Counter-Drone Technology
topics.summary: ACS discussed autonomous gun turrets as the key technology for defeating drone swarms; market is dominated by foreign companies like Rheinmetall and Kongsberg; autonomous guns will put downward pressure on expensive interceptors, lasers, and missiles.

topics.name: Hypersonic Aircraft Development
topics.summary: Hermeus discussed their iterative approach to building Mach 5 aircraft, achieving 15-month development for first prototype. Combined ramjet/turbojet engine demonstrated on the ground. Key insight: simplify the problem and only answer the specific question each prototype needs to answer.

topics.name: Defense Tech Supply Chain and Manufacturing Gap
topics.summary: The US defense industrial base relies on 1930s-1950s era machines and multi-generational workers. Critical components like remote weapon stations are mostly bought from foreign companies. Companies like Hadrian and Deterrence are addressing this, but CNC machines themselves must still be imported from Germany, South Korea, and Japan.

topics.name: AI in Manufacturing and Hard Tech
topics.summary: Discussed whether LLMs and generative AI models benefit hard tech; consensus is that physics-based manufacturing problems require proprietary training data. Companies like Atomic Industries are building their own models because no public training data exists for precision manufacturing.

topics.name: Silicon Valley vs. Defense Culture
topics.summary: Lengthy discussion on whether being a veteran or having military background gives investors and founders a genuine edge; consensus yes but technology moves so fast the edge erodes; talent aggregation in the early contrarian phase (2017-2022 for Anduril) was a key structural advantage now gone.
